## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

PRN Johor ke-16 concluded **11 July 2026** with BN winning a 48-seat supermajority. Policing was assessed as successful — KPN Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail confirmed 90 reports / 25 investigation papers during the 14-day campaign, none implicating candidates or senior party leaders, all minor offences (flag mischief/damage). Polling day proceeded smoothly with 14,000+ personnel deployed; no untoward incidents. Focus has now shifted to the **16th Negeri Sembilan state election** (polling day **1 Aug 2026**, early voting **28 July**), where PDRM has mobilised 200 KDNKA officers and opened 9 election-offence investigation papers as of 24 July. Separately, PDRM announced major non-election enforcement results: crippling of the "Vinod Gang" (Sosma, 11 arrested), a RM6.12mil marine meth seizure (Op Taring Gelora), and an arrest over an attempted cash-van robbery in Klang. No KDN/MOHA emergency directives, no phantom-voter findings, no polling-station security incidents detected.

## 2. ELECTION SECURITY

### 2.1 PRN Johor ke-16 — POST-ELECTION WRAP-UP (concluded)
- **Polling day:** 11 Jul 2026. Advance polling 7 Jul 2026.
- **Result:** BN 48 / 56 seats (supermajority). Voter turnout 69.57% (+14.65% vs 2022).
- **PDRM deployment:** ~14,000 officers/personnel across all 56 constituencies; 5,600+ from other contingents; PDRM Air Unit involved for aerial surveillance. (Earlier planning figure cited 11,926; final on-day figure 14,000+.)
- **Election-offence tally (FINAL — announced by IGP 11 Jul):** **90 police reports received, 25 investigation papers opened.** None implicated candidates or senior party leaders. Offences were minor — flag damage/removal/burning, mischief — and did not affect public order. *(Bernama, NST, The Vibes, The Edge — 11 Jul 2026)*
- **Progression of figures during campaign:**
  - 29 Jun: 3 IPs / 7 reports (Malay Mail)
  - 3 Jul: 8 IPs / 5 arson-related (Malay Mail)
  - 7 Jul: 18 IPs / 56 reports (NST, Bernama, The Sun)
  - 9 Jul: +4 IPs from 17 reports (The Star)
  - 11 Jul (final): 25 IPs / 90 reports (IGP)
- **KPN on the ground (11 Jul):** Visited SMK Taman Molek (11:45am), held press conference, visited SJK(C) Foon Yew 4 Larkin, then Bilik Full Manning PRN at IPK Johor for operational briefing. Quote: *"Setakat ini keadaan keselamatan di seluruh Johor berada dalam keadaan terkawal dan proses pengundian berjalan lancar."* *(rmp.gov.my news-detail, 13 Jul 2026)*
- **Phantom voters / electoral fraud:** No specific phantom-voter reports or fraud investigations surfaced in monitored sources for Johor.
- **Academic assessment:** RSIS Commentary No. 152 (15 Jul 2026, Ben Suffian/Merdeka Centre) — "Assessment and Early Analysis of the 2026 Johor State Election Results." Key: asymmetrical turnout (BN seats 65.7–68% vs PH urban ~60%), "Onn Hafiz Effect" (80% approval, 8% GDP growth, RM110bn investments), PN sat out 23 seats consolidating Malay vote, Indian voters ~60% to BN, DAP hit structural ceiling, BERSAMA (Rafizi Ramli) acted as spoiler in 4 seats. Federal unity-government stability now in question as UMNO gains leverage. *(rsis.edu.sg PDF)*

### 5.1 Major PDRM enforcement operations (non-election, Jul 23–24)
- **"Vinod Gang" crippled (Ops Rapido, 23–24 Jun; announced 23 Jul):** 11 members arrested, 5 at large. 17-member organised crime group, all Malaysian men 21–34, active since 2023, leader aged 30. 21 cases solved (armed robbery, attempted murder, rioting armed, hurt with weapons, mischief). Detained under **SOSMA**, charged under **Section 130V(1) Penal Code** (organised crime) at Sepang Sessions Court 24 Jul. *(Malay Mail, The Edge, NST, The Sun, Borneo Post — 23–24 Jul 2026)* — Spokesperson: **CID Director Datuk M. Kumar**.
- **Marine police meth seizure (Op Taring Gelora, 17 Jul; reported 24 Jul):** ~7nm south of Pulau Rimau, Penang. **113.776 kg syabu (RM5.69mil)** + 3,497 vape cartridges with liquid meth (6.3kg, RM315k) + fibre boat. Total **RM6.12mil**. Two Indonesian men (30, 51) arrested as sea transporters (RM10k each) ferrying Malaysia→Indonesia. Charged under Section 39B Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 (death/life). 7-day remand. *(The Star — 24 Jul 2026)* — Spokesperson: **Comm Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri (KDNKA Director)**.
- **Attempted cash-van robbery, Klang (incident 20 Jul; arrest 23 Jul; reported 24 Jul):** Local man in 20s arrested in Shah Alam. Recovered Mossberg pump-action shotgun (1 round), Ekol Lite starter pistol, 48 blank rounds. Investigated under Sections 392/397 Penal Code + Section 4 Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971. Remand under Section 117 CPC. *(Malay Mail — 24 Jul 2026)* — Spokesperson: **CID Director Datuk M. Kumar** (Bukit Aman CID D9 Division).
- **Bukit Mertajam human-trafficking syndicate probe (19 Jul):** MP Steven Sim called for comprehensive PDRM investigation into syndicate uncovered in Berapit. *(The Star — 19 Jul 2026)*
